stories.title: OKX funding-rate-history fetcher — settled series, interval derived from fundingTime deltas
stories.description:
As the owner, I want BTC's settled funding rate fetched with its interval derived from the
actual settlement history, so that annualising it later can never assume a cadence the
instrument doesn't currently have.

Research (`10-research.md`) is explicit about why this is the hard part of this PRD: OKX's
`public/funding-rate-history` endpoint returns the realized, settled rate per period — but
**no interval field**. The interval must be derived from the gap between consecutive settled
`fundingTime` values in the response itself. A practitioner guide published in 2026 and
surfaced in this project's own research hardcodes "8 hours" as a constant throughout its
examples — proof this is a live mistake being made in print, not a hypothetical one. OKX's
own settlement ladder (8h → 4h → 2h → 1h, and back, on a rolling 12-hour lookback near a
rate's cap or floor) means a single instrument can genuinely show more than one interval
within weeks.

This story fetches BTC only, proves the interval-derivation logic against real data, and
establishes the response contract the other three metrics' stories will reuse the pattern of.
Registering all four assets is US-602.

criteria.text: `public/funding-rate` is never called by this fetcher — only `public/funding-rate-history`

method.name: the fetcher returns the newest settled funding rate, never the live/predicted field

criteria.text: Never a hardcoded 8h/28800s constant anywhere in the computation path

method.name: the interval is computed from the delta between the two newest settled fundingTime values, in seconds

criteria.text: So a later change in this instrument's actual cadence is visible on the datapoint that measured it, not hidden behind a static description

method.name: the derived interval is recorded in the returned result's source-field text, distinct from the static registry source_field

criteria.text: An interval cannot be derived from a single point, and a single point silently treated as "no interval / assume default" is exactly the bug this story exists to prevent

method.name: fewer than two settled entries in the response is Error(FETCH_FAILED)

criteria.text: Same discipline as `okx.py` — the fetcher never raises past its own boundary

method.name: an HTTP error returns Error with the status code in the detail, and no value

criteria.text: `extra="forbid"` on the new `OkxFundingRateHistoryResponse` — an added, renamed, or retyped field fails loud, not silently ignored

method.name: a malformed or reshaped response is rejected by the response model

criteria.text: The direct F11 defence, same rule as every other fetcher in this project

method.name: source_timestamp is the newest settlement's fundingTime and is strictly in the past

criteria.text: Hits the real endpoint; this is what actually pins field names and shape, since research could not independently re-verify OKX's rubik/stat-adjacent docs page field-level detail

**Stack:** Python 3.12 (`uv`, httpx, pydantic, TA-Lib) ingestion · Supabase Postgres ·

> HTTP 451 to US IPs, which is what forced the prior system onto a self-hosted runner that
> later died silently. Do not assume GitHub-hosted runners can reach every venue — measure it.

**This product's one rule above all others:** it displays market data and **makes no
judgement about it**. No composite score, no signal, no ranking. A wrong number must look
different from a right one — that is the whole product. If a value cannot be honestly sourced
for an asset, it renders `UNAVAILABLE` with a reason, never a proxy and never `0`.

## How work happens here

This product runs on `uf`. Read `CYCLE.md` for the loop, `SKILLS.md` for which skill to fire

Work is organised as **PRDs** in `prds/PRD-00N-<slug>/`, walked in the order set by
`project-documents/05_Product_Roadmap.md`. Each PRD compiles to `spec.lock.json`, then runs
story by story: one agent implements in a fresh context, a **different vendor** verifies in
a read-only sandbox and must cite a file, line or test name per criterion.

**You cannot mark your own work complete.** Produce the evidence the criteria name — the
tests, the screenshots, the passing commands — and leave it where it can be found. Do not
write a summary claiming success; nobody reads it and the verifier ignores it.

```markdown
# 10-research.md — PRD-006-derivatives

## What we already knew, and whether it still holds

| Claim from our knowledge base | Still true? | What the source says | Citation |
|---|---|---|---|
| OKX is reachable from GitHub-hosted (US) runners; Binance and Bybit are not, for derivatives data | **Holds, and independently corroborated for Binance futures specifically** | A GCP US-IP user gets HTTP 451 from `fapi.binance.com` on unauthenticated, no-auth-needed public endpoints — "Any call to https://fapi.binance.com/fapi/(...) returns an HTTP 451 error," confirmed as IP-based geoblocking, not an account restriction | https://dev.binance.vision/t/error-451-when-accessing-the-futures-api-from-us/16725 |
| Funding intervals are dynamic and not fixed at 8h — OKX/Bybit can switch | **Holds, and now precisely characterized** — this PRD's central risk has an exact mechanism | OKX's automatic frequency adjustment: "When the funding rate reaches its cap or floor at settlement, the frequency will be escalated by one level at a time" — an explicit **8h → 4h → 2h → 1h** ladder, reverting only after "the funding rate at every settlement during the preceding 12 consecutive hours was within ±0.20%." OKX also manually re-tiered five named instruments from 8h to 4h in named 2024 announcements, independent of the automatic mechanism | https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/okx-to-enable-automatic-updates-for-funding-fee-settlement-period ; https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/okx-to-adjust-funding-rate-interval-for-certain-perpetual-futures |
| Vendors expose a live/predicted funding number distinct from settled funding, and blurring them is a trap | **Holds** — OKX's public docs and third-party engineering writeups treat `GET /public/funding-rate` (current + upcoming predicted rate) and `GET /public/funding-rate-history` (settled, historical) as genuinely separate endpoints with separate semantics | https://github.com/tiagosiebler/okx-api/blob/master/docs/endpointFunctionList.md |
| Coin-margined (inverse) vs USDT-margined (linear) OI is a unit-mixing trap | **Holds** | OKX names its non-USDT products "crypto-margined perpetual futures... settled in cryptocurrencies like BTC, with a contract size of 100 USD" against USDT-margined contracts settled in USDT — i.e. the same instrument family exists in both a coin-denominated and a USD-denominated form and nothing in the wire format stops you from summing across them | https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/i-perpetual-swaps (via search synthesis — see note below) |
| **Our knowledge base does NOT already know the exact endpoint the settlement interval must be read from** — it says "record it" but not where the source of truth is | **Gap, now closed** | There is **no dedicated field for "current interval" on the historical funding-rate-history payload itself**. OKX's own guidance for finding the *current* interval is to hit `GET /api/v5/public/funding-rate` (the live/predicted endpoint) or the web UI — "refer to the Perpetual Contract Information page or the API endpoint...for the latest settlement frequency, and adjust your trading strategies accordingly." The settled-history endpoint (`funding-rate-history`) returns only `fundingTime`/`fundingRate` per record — the interval for a *historical* record must be **derived from the gap between consecutive `fundingTime` values**, not read from a field | https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/okx-to-enable-automatic-updates-for-funding-fee-settlement-period |
| Long/short ratio and taker-ratio history depth may be capped (R1 flagged Binance's 30-day rolling cap; OKX's equivalent limit unconfirmed) | **Partially resolved, still a genuine open question** | Third-party SDK docs confirm OKX's `rubik/stat` family (open-interest-volume, taker-volume, long-short-account-ratio) all take `period`/`begin`/`end`/`limit` params, but no source found in this research pass states OKX's own retention ceiling in days. The parallel, better-documented `funding-rate-history` endpoint **is capped at 400 records** (≈1 year at 8h cadence) — this is the closest confirmed analog and the working assumption should be that `rubik/stat` endpoints have a comparable, not unlimited, retention window, to be confirmed empirically in the reachability spike rather than assumed | https://www.holysheep.cn/articles/en-okx-funding-rate-history-api-for-backtesting-2026-07-12-0017.html |

## Existing implementations

- **`tiagosiebler/okx-api`** (TypeScript, actively maintained, used widely as the reference for the full v5 surface) exposes each endpoint this PRD needs as a distinct typed function: `getFundingRate()`, `getFundingRateHistory()`, `getOpenInterest()`, `getContractsOpenInterestAndVolume()`, `getTakerVolume()`, `getContractTakerVolume()`, `getLongShortRatio()`, `getLongShortContractRatio()` — all public, no auth, GET-only. Confirms the shape this PRD's fetchers should mirror one endpoint per registry entry, not one combined call. https://github.com/tiagosiebler/okx-api/blob/master/docs/endpointFunctionList.md
- **`okxapi/python-okx`** — the Python reference SDK — hardcodes the same literal paths (`/api/v5/public/funding-rate`, `/api/v5/public/funding-rate-history`, `/api/v5/public/open-interest`, `/api/v5/rubik/stat/taker-volume`, `/api/v5/rubik/stat/contracts/long-short-account-ratio`) as constants, useful directly since this project's ingestion is already Python/httpx. https://github.com/okxapi/python-okx (consts.py)
- **HolySheep AI's backtesting engineering guide** is an existing practitioner writeup of exactly this PRD's funding-history ingestion problem: it hits `limit=100`/page, paginates on `fundingTime` via `after`, warns "OKX caps at 100/page" and that the total series is capped at "400 records (≈1 year for 8h funding cadence)," and separately warns that `before`/`after` pagination "is brittle for multi-symbol sweeps" — worth taking as a direct implementation constraint rather than re-discovering it via trial and error. https://www.holysheep.cn/articles/en-okx-funding-rate-history-api-for-backtesting-2026-07-12-0017.html

## Approach options

**A. OKX-only, single-venue, "uncorroborated" declared per US-306** — Fetch funding/OI/long-short/taker from OKX only, mark every derivatives registry entry as uncorroborated (structurally already legal per PRD-003/US-306). *Trade-off:* simplest, ships fastest, zero cross-venue reconciliation logic, but the registry carries a permanent "single source of truth" flag for this whole category — acceptable for a personal dashboard, not for anything claiming institutional-grade data quality. *Cost:* $0, one venue's rate limits only. *Who uses it:* small personal dashboards and single-exchange trading bots (implicit in every SDK surveyed — none of the surveyed OSS clients wrap more than one venue's derivatives endpoints in a single call).

**B. OKX primary + Coinglass (or similar aggregator) as second source for corroboration only** — OKX stays the fetched-and-displayed value; a second call to an aggregator checks the OKX number is in the same order of magnitude, without displaying the aggregator's (often modeled) number. *Trade-off:* satisfies US-306's "declare a second source" requirement with an actual second source rather than a flag, but Coinglass's own numbers for exactly this category (long/short, OI) are partly derived/modeled per this project's own prior finding on liquidations — using it even just for corroboration risks importing that same "modeled passing as measured" problem this PRD explicitly refuses. *Cost:* Coinglass free tier is rate-limited and its API terms/availability weren't verified in this pass — flag as **UNVERIFIED**, needs its own reachability check before committing. *Who uses it:* aggregator-dependent retail dashboards (Coinglass's own product is the canonical example of this pattern, per the coinglass.com references surfaced throughout this research pass, e.g. https://www.coinglass.com/exchanges/OKX).

**C. Two-venue direct: OKX + a genuinely reachable second exchange (e.g. Coinbase or Kraken derivatives, if they expose funding/OI at all), fully independent fetch-and-compare** — the gold-standard version of what PRD-003 asks for. *Trade-off:* Coinbase and Kraken's perpetual/derivatives products and public API surface for funding/OI/long-short were **not verified in this research pass** — this project's existing architecture doc only measured their *spot* OHLCV reachability, not their derivatives endpoints, so this option carries real unresolved risk that a second venue simply doesn't expose these fields publicly. *Cost:* unknown until endpoint existence is confirmed. *Who uses it:* institutional data vendors (Kaiko, Amberdata), not solo/small-team dashboards, per the general pattern across every practitioner source surveyed.

**Recommendation: Option A now, structured so Option B/C is a additive registry-entry change later.** Every source found in this pass — the SDK doc, the backtesting guide, OKX's own docs — treats OKX's derivatives surface as complete and self-consistent for BTC/ETH/SOL/BNB perpetuals; no second venue's derivatives endpoints were confirmed reachable or even existent in this research window, and PRD-003/US-306 already makes "declared uncorroborated" a legal, non-blocking state rather than a gap that has to be silently papered over.

## Edge cases and gotchas

- **The historical funding-rate endpoint carries no interval field — you must derive it from consecutive `fundingTime` deltas, or you will silently inherit the annualization bug this PRD exists to prevent.** OKX's own guidance for the *current* interval points to a *different* endpoint (`GET /public/funding-rate`, the live one this PRD deliberately does not fetch for display) or the web UI — nothing in the settled-history payload states the interval directly. A naive implementation that fetches `funding-rate-history` and assumes 8h will be wrong for exactly the tiered instruments OKX names by name. https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/okx-to-enable-automatic-updates-for-funding-fee-settlement-period
- **Backtesting-focused engineering writeups treating OKX in 2026 still hardcode "8h" without checking it.** The most detailed practitioner guide found in this pass — written specifically about funding-rate history for backtesting — states flatly "Funding rate — settled every 8 hours" as a fixed constant throughout its examples, with zero handling for interval changes. This is a live demonstration that the exact bug this PRD's adversarial case targets is not a hypothetical — a specialist writeup published in 2026 makes it. https://www.holysheep.cn/articles/en-okx-v5-api-yanshengpin-funding-rate-yu-mark-price--2026-07-18-0005.html
- **`funding-rate-history` is capped at 400 records total (≈1 year at 8h cadence), not a rolling window you can page through indefinitely, and pagination via `before`/`after` is "brittle for multi-symbol sweeps."** For BNB or other lower-liquidity instruments whose interval sometimes drops to 1h, 400 records covers far less real time than a year — the retention window is record-count-based, not time-based, so an instrument's own switch to a shorter interval silently shrinks its available history depth. https://www.holysheep.cn/articles/en-okx-funding-rate-history-api-for-backtesting-2026-07-12-0017.html
- **OKX's escalation ladder both tightens (8h→4h→2h→1h) *and* reverts, based on a rolling 12-hour lookback of settlements within ±0.20%** — meaning a single instrument can legitimately show 8h, 4h, 1h, then back to 8h within weeks. Any registry design that treats "funding interval" as a fixed per-instrument attribute set once at onboarding will drift stale silently. https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/okx-to-enable-automatic-updates-for-funding-fee-settlement-period
- **Binance's HTTP 451 to US IPs applies to unauthenticated, no-auth-required public market-data calls specifically on the futures/derivatives API (`fapi.binance.com`)**, not just trading/account endpoints — confirming this PRD cannot fall back to Binance for derivatives from the same US GitHub-hosted compute already chosen for the rest of the project, reinforcing rather than merely repeating the existing architecture decision. https://dev.binance.vision/t/error-451-when-accessing-the-futures-api-from-us/16725

## Services and keys this PRD needs

| Service | Why | Env var | Already provisioned? |
|---|---|---|---|
| OKX public API | Funding rate (settled), OI, long/short ratio, taker ratio — all public, no auth required per every SDK surveyed | none required (public endpoints) | Yes — already integrated for spot/OHLCV per current architecture |

No new keys or secrets are needed for Option A (OKX-only). If Option B/C is later adopted for a second corroboration venue, that venue's key/rate-limit requirements are unverified and must be researched separately before being added here.

## Open questions for the human

| Question | My hypothesis | Impact if wrong | Rank |
|---|---|---|---|
| Does OKX's `rubik/stat` family (OI-volume, taker-volume, long-short-ratio) have a documented retention ceiling, or is it genuinely unbounded? | **UNVERIFIED** hypothesis: it mirrors `funding-rate-history`'s pattern of a hard record-count cap rather than being unbounded, likely on the order of a year or less at the shortest available `period` granularity — must be confirmed empirically against the live endpoint before backfill design is finalized | If wrong (endpoint is actually unbounded), the backfill design is unnecessarily conservative — low cost. If wrong the other way (cap is much shorter than assumed), a backfill story could silently under-deliver history depth without erroring | 1 |
| Should the board standardize on USDT-margined (linear) perpetuals for all four assets, given BNB has no natively obvious coin-margined equivalent anyway? | Yes — USDT-margined for BTC/ETH/SOL/BNB uniformly, since it's the more liquid, more uniformly-available product line across all four assets and avoids the coin/USD unit-mixing trap by construction rather than by validation | If wrong, some instrument's OI values are silently in a different denomination than the other three, defeating the registry-note discipline this PRD calls for | 2 |
| Is a second venue for derivatives corroboration reachable at all from GitHub-hosted US compute, or does US-306's "declare uncorroborated" apply to the whole category permanently? | Uncorroborated-and-declared (Option A) for v1 — no second venue's derivatives public endpoints were confirmed to exist, let alone be reachable, in this research pass | If a second venue turns out to be trivially available later, this is a missed cheap win, not a correctness risk — low cost either way | 3 |

## Blind spots

1. **The registry's "funding interval" field will be correct at write-time and wrong by the next fetch if the escalation/de-escalation ladder isn't re-checked on every ingest, not just at onboarding.** OKX's mechanism explicitly reverts after 12 hours of stable settlements — a field set once and never re-derived from live `fundingTime` deltas will drift the same way the prior system's "confident 0.0" drifted, just more subtly, because it will look plausible rather than obviously blank.
2. **`rubik/stat` endpoints (OI-volume, long-short-ratio, taker-volume) were not confirmed in this research pass to distinguish linear from inverse contracts in their response payload the same way `open-interest`/instrument IDs do.** If the aggregate stat endpoints blend `instType=SWAP` across both margin types under the hood — which was not ruled out here — the unit-mixing trap this PRD names explicitly for raw OI could reappear one layer up, inside an OKX-computed ratio the fetcher never gets to inspect or split.
3. **Nobody has checked whether OKX's rate limits on the `rubik/stat` family (distinct from the 20 req/s figure confirmed only for the public funding endpoint) can sustain four assets × four metrics on the existing GitHub Actions cron cadence without throttling** — a throttling failure here would not look like an outage, it would look like intermittently missing rows, which is exactly the failure mode PRD-005's completeness matrix was built to catch, but only if this PRD's fetchers report it as missing rather than silently retrying into a 429 that gets treated as a transient error and dropped.

## Sources

- https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/okx-to-enable-automatic-updates-for-funding-fee-settlement-period
- https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/okx-to-adjust-funding-rate-interval-for-certain-perpetual-futures
- https://dev.binance.vision/t/error-451-when-accessing-the-futures-api-from-us/16725
- https://www.holysheep.cn/articles/en-okx-funding-rate-history-api-for-backtesting-2026-07-12-0017.html
- https://www.holysheep.cn/articles/en-okx-v5-api-yanshengpin-funding-rate-yu-mark-price--2026-07-18-0005.html
- https://github.com/tiagosiebler/okx-api/blob/master/docs/endpointFunctionList.md
- https://github.com/okxapi/python-okx (consts.py)
- https://www.okx.com/docs-v5/log_en/
- https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/i-perpetual-swaps
```

# 11 · Data model

The compact, authoritative design. Distilled from `research/R5-data-integrity-engineering.md`
and `research/R0-lessons-from-prior-system.md` so stories can inline this instead of the full
research. Where this conflicts with a research file, **this file wins** — it is the decision.

---

## The one rule

**A wrong number must look different from a right one.** Everything below exists to make that
structurally true rather than a matter of discipline.

## 1. Status is a type, not a convention

Four outcomes, modelled as a discriminated union of frozen dataclasses — never one class with
optional fields:

```
Ok(value, source_timestamp)          # we have it, and it is current
Stale(value, source_timestamp)       # we have it, but it is past its freshness budget
Unavailable(reason)                  # we do not have it, and here is why
Error(reason, detail)                # the attempt failed
```

`Unavailable` and `Error` **have no `value` attribute at all**. Reading one is an
`AttributeError`, not a zero.

**Forbidden:** any helper that converts absence back to a number — `.value_or(0.0)`,
`.as_float()`, `or 0`, `fillna(0)`, a neutral default. This is the exact mechanism by which
the prior system's funding rate, open interest and long/short ratio reported a confident
`0.0` for months because a fetcher was never called.

### 1.1 Three kinds of absence, kept distinct

```
NOT_DEFINABLE   the metric has no meaning on this chain and never will
                (SOPR/MVRV on Solana: account-based, no UTXO to timestamp).
                Not purchasable at any price. Permanent, and correct.
PAYWALLED       exists, we lack credentials (realized cap on Coin Metrics free)
FETCH_FAILED    should exist, did not arrive — timeout, 500, empty after filtering
NOT_FETCHED     the pipeline never attempted it
```

`NOT_FETCHED` is the default state of every indicator at the start of a run. It exists so that
"never ran" and "ran and got nothing" are different rows. Collapsing these four into one blank
cell destroys the information the owner most needs: whether a gap is permanent, purchasable,
broken, or a bug.

## 2. Schema

```sql
CREATE TYPE datapoint_status  AS ENUM ('OK','STALE','UNAVAILABLE','ERROR');
CREATE TYPE unavailable_reason AS ENUM ('NOT_DEFINABLE','PAYWALLED','FETCH_FAILED','NOT_FETCHED');

CREATE TABLE datapoints (
  id               bigserial PRIMARY KEY,
  indicator_key    text NOT NULL,          -- FK in spirit to the registry
  asset            text NOT NULL,          -- what we DISPLAY it as
  measured_on      text NOT NULL,          -- what it was ACTUALLY measured on
  value            double precision,       -- NULL unless status IN ('OK','STALE')
  status           datapoint_status NOT NULL,
  reason           unavailable_reason,
  source_vendor    text NOT NULL,
  endpoint         text NOT NULL,
  source_field     text NOT NULL,          -- WHICH FIELD of the response
  fetched_at       timestamptz NOT NULL,   -- when WE fetched
  source_timestamp timestamptz,            -- when the SOURCE says it is as-of
  CONSTRAINT asset_match     CHECK (status <> 'OK' OR measured_on = asset),
  CONSTRAINT value_iff_ok    CHECK ((status IN ('OK','STALE')) = (value IS NOT NULL)),
  CONSTRAINT reason_required CHECK ((status IN ('UNAVAILABLE','ERROR')) = (reason IS NOT NULL))
);

CREATE INDEX ON datapoints (indicator_key, asset, fetched_at DESC);
```

**Long and narrow, never wide.** The prior system stored one column pair per indicator
(`ls_ratio_score`, `oi_raw`, …), so adding an indicator required a migration and its integrity
check covered exactly two hardcoded rows while drifting from reality unnoticed. Here a new
indicator is a row.

### Why each constraint exists

| Constraint | Prevents |
|---|---|
| `asset_match` | BTC's MVRV displayed as SOL's. The prior system did this to 8 coins and called the result *"not degraded data, wrong data"*. Now a **database error** |
| `value_iff_ok` | Status and value drifting apart — a value with no status, or an `OK` with nothing in it |
| `reason_required` | Absence that does not say why |

A mismatched row **may** be inserted as `UNAVAILABLE` for audit. The constraint only forbids
it carrying `OK`. Recording that we fetched the wrong thing is useful; displaying it as
correct is not.

### Two timestamps, two owners

`fetched_at` is set by the **writer**. `source_timestamp` is set by the **fetcher**, from the
source's own as-of time. They answer different questions and must never be conflated.

**A `source_timestamp` in the future is an error, not a value.** The prior system read funding
from `premiumIndex.lastFundingRate` — a continuously-moving estimate for an *upcoming*
settlement — instead of the settled series, and stored it as history. Measured: `0.00002925`
against a settled `0.00003113`, on a number that keeps drifting. This assertion is what makes
that class of bug impossible.

## 3. Registry — one declarative source of truth

```yaml
- key: btc_daily_close
  vendor: okx
  endpoint: https://www.okx.com/api/v5/market/candles?instId=BTC-USDT&bar=1D
  source_field: 'candle[4] (close), where candle[8] == "1"'
  definable_for: [BTC]
  expected_update_interval_seconds: 86400
  freshness_warn_seconds:  108000   # 30h
  freshness_stale_seconds: 172800   # 48h
```

- **`source_field` is mandatory.** Recording only the endpoint is how the funding-rate bug
  stayed invisible — right endpoint, wrong field.
- **`definable_for` is about meaning, not availability**, and a wildcard is rejected. An
  indicator must state which assets it is genuinely valid for.
- Integrity coverage is **generated from this registry**, so an indicator with no coverage is
  a build error rather than an oversight.
- The registry is blast-radius: changing an entry retroactively changes the meaning of every
  stored value carrying that key.

## 4. Freshness — three numbers, not one

| Field | Question it answers |
|---|---|
| `expected_update_interval` | how often the source *publishes* |
| `freshness_warn` | when to flag it visually (≈1.5× interval) |
| `freshness_stale` | when it becomes `STALE` (≈2× interval) |

Two thresholds survive one missed cycle without crying wolf, and catch two. A daily-close
indicator: interval 24h, warn 30h, stale 48h.

**Frozen is a separate check.** A source can be *fresh* — `fetched_at` seconds ago — while
returning an identical payload forever. Detecting that means comparing against the last N
stored values, and it is PRD-009. PRD-001 only provides the columns that make it possible.

## 4b. Reference period vs published date

**The timestamp a value describes is not the timestamp at which it became knowable.** Measured
against the live FRED API on 2026-09-08:

| Series | Latest observation | Days behind that day |
|---|---|---|
| `DFF` (Fed funds) | 2026-09-03 | 5 |
| `DTWEXBGS` (broad USD) | 2026-08-28 | 11 |
| `M2SL` (M2) | 2026-07-01 | **69** |

`M2SL` is a *monthly* series: the July figure is the newest that exists, and it was published
weeks after July ended. Displaying `23218` as today's M2 is false in two separate ways — wrong
period, and silent about the delay.

So a lagged indicator carries **two** timestamps, not one:

- `reference_period` — the period the value describes (July 2026)
- `source_timestamp` / `published_at` — when it became knowable

The UI shows both, and the freshness budget is computed against **publication**, not the
reference period — otherwise every monthly series is permanently `STALE` by construction.

This generalises past macro: funding rate (settled vs predicted), ETF flows (T+1), an unclosed
daily candle, and CPI are all the same shape. `ai-hedge-fund` reached it independently and
enforces it by filtering on `filing_date` rather than `report_period`, because the latter
"leaks 3-6 weeks of future" (R9 §2).

## 4c. Corroboration — disagreement is a finding, not a problem to resolve

Every other rule in this document defends against a failure someone predicted. Corroboration is
the only one that catches a wrong number **nobody thought to check for**, and it is therefore
the most valuable single mechanism here. Designed in PRD-003.

The shape: fetch the same quantity from two or more independent venues, compare, and record the
comparison.

**The trap to avoid:** silently picking a winner. Averaging two disagreeing sources, or
preferring the "primary" one, throws away the only signal that something is wrong and produces
a confident number — which is exactly the failure mode this product exists to eliminate. If two
venues disagree beyond tolerance, **that is the finding**, and it must reach the face of the
value.

Concretely:

- The measured OKX case is the worked example. `bar=1D` (Hong Kong day) gave **78,834.1**;
  `bar=1Dutc` gave **79,111.8** — 0.35% apart. Comparing OKX against Coinbase would have
  flagged it automatically on day one. Instead it was caught because a person read the
  timestamp. That is not a repeatable defence.
- Tolerance is per-indicator and belongs in the registry, not hardcoded. Spot close across major
  venues sits far tighter than, say, aggregated open interest. R5 flagged a specific numeric
  tolerance as **UNVERIFIED** — it must be measured from observed spreads, not guessed.
- Divergence needs its own visible state. Whether that is a new `reason` value, a separate
  `corroboration` column, or a companion row is a PRD-003 decision; what is settled here is that
  it may not be silently swallowed, and that a corroborated value and an uncorroborated one must
  not look identical.
- Corroboration is not available for everything. A metric published by exactly one vendor
  (Coin Metrics MVRV) has no second opinion, and that fact should itself be visible rather than
  implied.

## 4d. Warm-up: measured, not assumed

**A recursive indicator's value depends on how much history preceded it.** Measured 2026-09-10
on 599 real OKX BTC daily closes — the *same final bar*, RSI(14), varying only the length of
history supplied:

| bars supplied | RSI(14) | drift vs converged |
|---|---|---|
| 15 | 47.56 | −11.94 |
| 20 | 48.62 | −10.88 |
| 30 | **63.90** | **+4.40** |
| 50 | 58.98 | −0.52 |
| 100 | 59.51 | +0.008 |
| 150 → 500 | **59.4972** | **0.0000** |

A **16-point spread on a 0–100 oscillator** — the difference between reading oversold and
overbought — with no error, no NaN and a plausible number at every length. This is the prior
system's *"same market, different score"* reproduced exactly, in TA-Lib.

**Two traps this exposes:**

1. **TA-Lib's own `lookback` is not a warm-up figure.** It reports RSI 14, ATR 14, MACD 33,
   STOCHRSI 20, EMA(200) 199. Those are the *mechanical floor* — the inputs consumed before any
   output exists. Taking them as `required_bars` gives RSI 14 bars and a value 12 points wrong.
2. **The unstable period defaults to 0**, so TA-Lib strips nothing and warns nothing. A 30-bar
   RSI array returns a confident float at index 14.

**Therefore:** recursive indicators (RSI, ATR, EMA, StochRSI, **and MACD**, which TA-Lib does
*not* annotate despite its EMA-26 core) declare **250 bars**. Convergence arrives near 150 in
this measurement; 250 is deliberate headroom. Non-recursive indicators (Bollinger, OBV) declare
their own smaller honest N.

The exactly-N contract from PRD-002 is what makes this safe: a cache growing from 30 bars to 150
would otherwise walk RSI from 63.9 to 59.5 over weeks, silently.

## 5. Fallbacks are different indicators

If a value cannot be obtained from its declared source, the answer is `UNAVAILABLE` — **not a
substitute source under the same label.** The prior system silently swapped FRED's `DTWEXBGS`
(26 currencies, weekly, lagged) for yfinance's `DX-Y.NYB` (6 currencies, real-time) behind one
"DXY" label; the value jumped discontinuously whenever the fallback engaged and nothing
recorded which had produced it.

A second source is a second registry entry with its own key, displayed as its own series, or
it does not exist.

## 6. Rendering

TypeScript mirrors the union, with an exhaustive `switch` and a `never` fallthrough so an
unhandled status is a **compile error**:

```ts
type Datapoint =
  | { status: "OK";          value: number; sourceTimestamp: string }
  | { status: "STALE";       value: number; sourceTimestamp: string }
  | { status: "UNAVAILABLE"; reason: Reason }
  | { status: "ERROR";       reason: Reason; detail: string };
```

- `UNAVAILABLE` renders an em dash and its reason. **Never `0`. Never blank.**
- `STALE` renders the value **with its age and a visible stale treatment** — shown, but never
  shown as if current.
- Provenance (vendor, endpoint, source timestamp) is on the face of the value, not behind a
  click.
- No "last known good" fallback that silently presents an older value as current.

# Mobile & PWA

> Mobile & PWA is the layer that extends a web product onto phones and tablets, either by making your existing site installable and offline-capable (a Progressive Web App) or by shipping a real app to the Apple App Store and Google Play built from a shared codebase (React Native, Expo, Flutter, Capacitor, etc.). # 10-research.md — PRD-006-derivatives

```markdown
## What we already knew, and whether it still holds

| Claim from our knowledge base | Still true? | What the source says | Citation |
|---|---|---|---|
| OKX is reachable from GitHub-hosted (US) runners; Binance and Bybit are not, for derivatives data | **Holds, and independently corroborated for Binance futures specifically** | A GCP US-IP user gets HTTP 451 from `fapi.binance.com` on unauthenticated, no-auth-needed public endpoints — "Any call to https://fapi.binance.com/fapi/(...) returns an HTTP 451 error," confirmed as IP-based geoblocking, not an account restriction | https://dev.binance.vision/t/error-451-when-accessing-the-futures-api-from-us/16725 |
| Funding intervals are dynamic and not fixed at 8h — OKX/Bybit can switch | **Holds, and now precisely characterized** — this PRD's central risk has an exact mechanism | OKX's automatic frequency adjustment: "When the funding rate reaches its cap or floor at settlement, the frequency will be escalated by one level at a time" — an explicit **8h → 4h → 2h → 1h** ladder, reverting only after "the funding rate at every settlement during the preceding 12 consecutive hours was within ±0.20%." OKX also manually re-tiered five named instruments from 8h to 4h in named 2024 announcements, independent of the automatic mechanism | https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/okx-to-enable-automatic-updates-for-funding-fee-settlement-period ; https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/okx-to-adjust-funding-rate-interval-for-certain-perpetual-futures |
| Vendors expose a live/predicted funding number distinct from settled funding, and blurring them is a trap | **Holds** — OKX's public docs and third-party engineering writeups treat `GET /public/funding-rate` (current + upcoming predicted rate) and `GET /public/funding-rate-history` (settled, historical) as genuinely separate endpoints with separate semantics | https://github.com/tiagosiebler/okx-api/blob/master/docs/endpointFunctionList.md |
| Coin-margined (inverse) vs USDT-margined (linear) OI is a unit-mixing trap | **Holds** | OKX names its non-USDT products "crypto-margined perpetual futures... settled in cryptocurrencies like BTC, with a contract size of 100 USD" against USDT-margined contracts settled in USDT — i.e. the same instrument family exists in both a coin-denominated and a USD-denominated form and nothing in the wire format stops you from summing across them | https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/i-perpetual-swaps (via search synthesis — see note below) |
| **Our knowledge base does NOT already know the exact endpoint the settlement interval must be read from** — it says "record it" but not where the source of truth is | **Gap, now closed** | There is **no dedicated field for "current interval" on the historical funding-rate-history payload itself**. OKX's own guidance for finding the *current* interval is to hit `GET /api/v5/public/funding-rate` (the live/predicted endpoint) or the web UI — "refer to the Perpetual Contract Information page or the API endpoint...for the latest settlement frequency, and adjust your trading strategies accordingly." The settled-history endpoint (`funding-rate-history`) returns only `fundingTime`/`fundingRate` per record — the interval for a *historical* record must be **derived from the gap between consecutive `fundingTime` values**, not read from a field | https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/okx-to-enable-automatic-updates-for-funding-fee-settlement-period |
| Long/short ratio and taker-ratio history depth may be capped (R1 flagged Binance's 30-day rolling cap; OKX's equivalent limit unconfirmed) | **Partially resolved, still a genuine open question** | Third-party SDK docs confirm OKX's `rubik/stat` family (open-interest-volume, taker-volume, long-short-account-ratio) all take `period`/`begin`/`end`/`limit` params, but no source found in this research pass states OKX's own retention ceiling in days. The parallel, better-documented `funding-rate-history` endpoint **is capped at 400 records** (≈1 year at 8h cadence) — this is the closest confirmed analog and the working assumption should be that `rubik/stat` endpoints have a comparable, not unlimited, retention window, to be confirmed empirically in the reachability spike rather than assumed | https://www.holysheep.cn/articles/en-okx-funding-rate-history-api-for-backtesting-2026-07-12-0017.html |

## Existing implementations

- **`tiagosiebler/okx-api`** (TypeScript, actively maintained, used widely as the reference for the full v5 surface) exposes each endpoint this PRD needs as a distinct typed function: `getFundingRate()`, `getFundingRateHistory()`, `getOpenInterest()`, `getContractsOpenInterestAndVolume()`, `getTakerVolume()`, `getContractTakerVolume()`, `getLongShortRatio()`, `getLongShortContractRatio()` — all public, no auth, GET-only. Confirms the shape this PRD's fetchers should mirror one endpoint per registry entry, not one combined call. https://github.com/tiagosiebler/okx-api/blob/master/docs/endpointFunctionList.md
- **`okxapi/python-okx`** — the Python reference SDK — hardcodes the same literal paths (`/api/v5/public/funding-rate`, `/api/v5/public/funding-rate-history`, `/api/v5/public/open-interest`, `/api/v5/rubik/stat/taker-volume`, `/api/v5/rubik/stat/contracts/long-short-account-ratio`) as constants, useful directly since this project's ingestion is already Python/httpx. https://github.com/okxapi/python-okx (consts.py)
- **HolySheep AI's backtesting engineering guide** is an existing practitioner writeup of exactly this PRD's funding-history ingestion problem: it hits `limit=100`/page, paginates on `fundingTime` via `after`, warns "OKX caps at 100/page" and that the total series is capped at "400 records (≈1 year for 8h funding cadence)," and separately warns that `before`/`after` pagination "is brittle for multi-symbol sweeps" — worth taking as a direct implementation constraint rather than re-discovering it via trial and error. https://www.holysheep.cn/articles/en-okx-funding-rate-history-api-for-backtesting-2026-07-12-0017.html

## Approach options

**A. OKX-only, single-venue, "uncorroborated" declared per US-306** — Fetch funding/OI/long-short/taker from OKX only, mark every derivatives registry entry as uncorroborated (structurally already legal per PRD-003/US-306). *Trade-off:* simplest, ships fastest, zero cross-venue reconciliation logic, but the registry carries a permanent "single source of truth" flag for this whole category — acceptable for a personal dashboard, not for anything claiming institutional-grade data quality. *Cost:* $0, one venue's rate limits only. *Who uses it:* small personal dashboards and single-exchange trading bots (implicit in every SDK surveyed — none of the surveyed OSS clients wrap more than one venue's derivatives endpoints in a single call).

**B. OKX primary + Coinglass (or similar aggregator) as second source for corroboration only** — OKX stays the fetched-and-displayed value; a second call to an aggregator checks the OKX number is in the same order of magnitude, without displaying the aggregator's (often modeled) number. *Trade-off:* satisfies US-306's "declare a second source" requirement with an actual second source rather than a flag, but Coinglass's own numbers for exactly this category (long/short, OI) are partly derived/modeled per this project's own prior finding on liquidations — using it even just for corroboration risks importing that same "modeled passing as measured" problem this PRD explicitly refuses. *Cost:* Coinglass free tier is rate-limited and its API terms/availability weren't verified in this pass — flag as **UNVERIFIED**, needs its own reachability check before committing. *Who uses it:* aggregator-dependent retail dashboards (Coinglass's own product is the canonical example of this pattern, per the coinglass.com references surfaced throughout this research pass, e.g. https://www.coinglass.com/exchanges/OKX).

**C. Two-venue direct: OKX + a genuinely reachable second exchange (e.g. Coinbase or Kraken derivatives, if they expose funding/OI at all), fully independent fetch-and-compare** — the gold-standard version of what PRD-003 asks for. *Trade-off:* Coinbase and Kraken's perpetual/derivatives products and public API surface for funding/OI/long-short were **not verified in this research pass** — this project's existing architecture doc only measured their *spot* OHLCV reachability, not their derivatives endpoints, so this option carries real unresolved risk that a second venue simply doesn't expose these fields publicly. *Cost:* unknown until endpoint existence is confirmed. *Who uses it:* institutional data vendors (Kaiko, Amberdata), not solo/small-team dashboards, per the general pattern across every practitioner source surveyed.

**Recommendation: Option A now, structured so Option B/C is a additive registry-entry change later.** Every source found in this pass — the SDK doc, the backtesting guide, OKX's own docs — treats OKX's derivatives surface as complete and self-consistent for BTC/ETH/SOL/BNB perpetuals; no second venue's derivatives endpoints were confirmed reachable or even existent in this research window, and PRD-003/US-306 already makes "declared uncorroborated" a legal, non-blocking state rather than a gap that has to be silently papered over.

## Edge cases and gotchas
```

# 11 · Data model

The compact, authoritative design. Distilled from `research/R5-data-integrity-engineering.md`
and `research/R0-lessons-from-prior-system.md` so stories can inline this instead of the full
research. Where this conflicts with a research file, **this file wins** — it is the decision.

---

## The one rule

**A wrong number must look different from a right one.** Everything below exists to make that
structurally true rather than a matter of discipline.

## 1. Status is a type, not a convention

Four outcomes, modelled as a discriminated union of frozen dataclasses — never one class with
optional fields:

```
Ok(value, source_timestamp)          # we have it, and it is current
Stale(value, source_timestamp)       # we have it, but it is past its freshness budget
Unavailable(reason)                  # we do not have it, and here is why
Error(reason, detail)                # the attempt failed
```

`Unavailable` and `Error` **have no `value` attribute at all**. Reading one is an
`AttributeError`, not a zero.

**Forbidden:** any helper that converts absence back to a number — `.value_or(0.0)`,
`.as_float()`, `or 0`, `fillna(0)`, a neutral default. This is the exact mechanism by which
the prior system's funding rate, open interest and long/short ratio reported a confident
`0.0` for months because a fetcher was never called.

### 1.1 Three kinds of absence, kept distinct

```
NOT_DEFINABLE   the metric has no meaning on this chain and never will
                (SOPR/MVRV on Solana: account-based, no UTXO to timestamp).
                Not purchasable at any price. Permanent, and correct.
PAYWALLED       exists, we lack credentials (realized cap on Coin Metrics free)
FETCH_FAILED    should exist, did not arrive — timeout, 500, empty after filtering
NOT_FETCHED     the pipeline never attempted it
```

`NOT_FETCHED` is the default state of every indicator at the start of a run. It exists so that
"never ran" and "ran and got nothing" are different rows. Collapsing these four into one blank
cell destroys the information the owner most needs: whether a gap is permanent, purchasable,
broken, or a bug.

## 2. Schema

```sql
CREATE TYPE datapoint_status  AS ENUM ('OK','STALE','UNAVAILABLE','ERROR');
CREATE TYPE unavailable_reason AS ENUM ('NOT_DEFINABLE','PAYWALLED','FETCH_FAILED','NOT_FETCHED');

CREATE TABLE datapoints (
  id               bigserial PRIMARY KEY,
  indicator_key    text NOT NULL,          -- FK in spirit to the registry
  asset            text NOT NULL,          -- what we DISPLAY it as
  measured_on      text NOT NULL,          -- what it was ACTUALLY measured on
  value            double precision,       -- NULL unless status IN ('OK','STALE')
  status           datapoint_status NOT NULL,
  reason           unavailable_reason,
  source_vendor    text NOT NULL,
  endpoint         text NOT NULL,
  source_field     text NOT NULL,          -- WHICH FIELD of the response
  fetched_at       timestamptz NOT NULL,   -- when WE fetched
  source_timestamp timestamptz,            -- when the SOURCE says it is as-of
  CONSTRAINT asset_match     CHECK (status <> 'OK' OR measured_on = asset),
  CONSTRAINT value_iff_ok    CHECK ((status IN ('OK','STALE')) = (value IS NOT NULL)),
  CONSTRAINT reason_required CHECK ((status IN ('UNAVAILABLE','ERROR')) = (reason IS NOT NULL))
);

CREATE INDEX ON datapoints (indicator_key, asset, fetched_at DESC);
```

**Long and narrow, never wide.** The prior system stored one column pair per indicator
(`ls_ratio_score`, `oi_raw`, …), so adding an indicator required a migration and its integrity
check covered exactly two hardcoded rows while drifting from reality unnoticed. Here a new
indicator is a row.

### Why each constraint exists

| Constraint | Prevents |
|---|---|
| `asset_match` | BTC's MVRV displayed as SOL's. The prior system did this to 8 coins and called the result *"not degraded data, wrong data"*. Now a **database error** |
| `value_iff_ok` | Status and value drifting apart — a value with no status, or an `OK` with nothing in it |
| `reason_required` | Absence that does not say why |

A mismatched row **may** be inserted as `UNAVAILABLE` for audit. The constraint only forbids
it carrying `OK`. Recording that we fetched the wrong thing is useful; displaying it as
correct is not.

### Two timestamps, two owners

`fetched_at` is set by the **writer**. `source_timestamp` is set by the **fetcher**, from the
source's own as-of time. They answer different questions and must never be conflated.

**A `source_timestamp` in the future is an error, not a value.** The prior system read funding
from `premiumIndex.lastFundingRate` — a continuously-moving estimate for an *upcoming*
settlement — instead of the settled series, and stored it as history. Measured: `0.00002925`
against a settled `0.00003113`, on a number that keeps drifting. This assertion is what makes
that class of bug impossible.

## 3. Registry — one declarative source of truth

```yaml
- key: btc_daily_close
  vendor: okx
  endpoint: https://www.okx.com/api/v5/market/candles?instId=BTC-USDT&bar=1D
  source_field: 'candle[4] (close), where candle[8] == "1"'
  definable_for: [BTC]
  expected_update_interval_seconds: 86400
  freshness_warn_seconds:  108000   # 30h
  freshness_stale_seconds: 172800   # 48h
```

- **`source_field` is mandatory.** Recording only the endpoint is how the funding-rate bug
  stayed invisible — right endpoint, wrong field.
- **`definable_for` is about meaning, not availability**, and a wildcard is rejected. An
  indicator must state which assets it is genuinely valid for.
- Integrity coverage is **generated from this registry**, so an indicator with no coverage is
  a build error rather than an oversight.
- The registry is blast-radius: changing an entry retroactively changes the meaning of every
  stored value carrying that key.

## 4. Freshness — three numbers, not one

| Field | Question it answers |
|---|---|
| `expected_update_interval` | how often the source *publishes* |
| `freshness_warn` | when to flag it visually (≈1.5× interval) |
| `freshness_stale` | when it becomes `STALE` (≈2× interval) |

Two thresholds survive one missed cycle without crying wolf, and catch two. A daily-close
indicator: interval 24h, warn 30h, stale 48h.

**Frozen is a separate check.** A source can be *fresh* — `fetched_at` seconds ago — while
returning an identical payload forever. Detecting that means comparing against the last N
stored values, and it is PRD-009. PRD-001 only provides the columns that make it possible.

## 4b. Reference period vs published date

**The timestamp a value describes is not the timestamp at which it became knowable.** Measured
against the live FRED API on 2026-09-08:

| Series | Latest observation | Days behind that day |
|---|---|---|
| `DFF` (Fed funds) | 2026-09-03 | 5 |
| `DTWEXBGS` (broad USD) | 2026-08-28 | 11 |
| `M2SL` (M2) | 2026-07-01 | **69** |

`M2SL` is a *monthly* series: the July figure is the newest that exists, and it was published
weeks after July ended. Displaying `23218` as today's M2 is false in two separate ways — wrong
period, and silent about the delay.

So a lagged indicator carries **two** timestamps, not one:

- `reference_period` — the period the value describes (July 2026)
- `source_timestamp` / `published_at` — when it became knowable

The UI shows both, and the freshness budget is computed against **publication**, not the
reference period — otherwise every monthly series is permanently `STALE` by construction.

This generalises past macro: funding rate (settled vs predicted), ETF flows (T+1), an unclosed
daily candle, and CPI are all the same shape. `ai-hedge-fund` reached it independently and
enforces it by filtering on `filing_date` rather than `report_period`, because the latter
"leaks 3-6 weeks of future" (R9 §2).

## 4c. Corroboration — disagreement is a finding, not a problem to resolve

Every other rule in this document defends against a failure someone predicted. Corroboration is
the only one that catches a wrong number **nobody thought to check for**, and it is therefore
the most valuable single mechanism here. Designed in PRD-003.

The shape: fetch the same quantity from two or more independent venues, compare, and record the
comparison.

**The trap to avoid:** silently picking a winner. Averaging two disagreeing sources, or
preferring the "primary" one, throws away the only signal that something is wrong and produces
a confident number — which is exactly the failure mode this product exists to eliminate. If two
venues disagree beyond tolerance, **that is the finding**, and it must reach the face of the
value.

Concretely:

- The measured OKX case is the worked example. `bar=1D` (Hong Kong day) gave **78,834.1**;
  `bar=1Dutc` gave **79,111.8** — 0.35% apart. Comparing OKX against Coinbase would have
  flagged it automatically on day one. Instead it was caught because a person read the
  timestamp. That is not a repeatable defence.
- Tolerance is per-indicator and belongs in the registry, not hardcoded. Spot close across major
  venues sits far tighter than, say, aggregated open interest. R5 flagged a specific numeric
  tolerance as **UNVERIFIED** — it must be measured from observed spreads, not guessed.
- Divergence needs its own visible state. Whether that is a new `reason` value, a separate
  `corroboration` column, or a companion row is a PRD-003 decision; what is settled here is that
  it may not be silently swallowed, and that a corroborated value and an uncorroborated one must
  not look identical.
- Corroboration is not available for everything. A metric published by exactly one vendor
  (Coin Metrics MVRV) has no second opinion, and that fact should itself be visible rather than
  implied.

## 4d. Warm-up: measured, not assumed

**A recursive indicator's value depends on how much history preceded it.** Measured 2026-09-10
on 599 real OKX BTC daily closes — the *same final bar*, RSI(14), varying only the length of
history supplied:

| bars supplied | RSI(14) | drift vs converged |
|---|---|---|
| 15 | 47.56 | −11.94 |
| 20 | 48.62 | −10.88 |
| 30 | **63.90** | **+4.40** |
| 50 | 58.98 | −0.52 |
| 100 | 59.51 | +0.008 |
| 150 → 500 | **59.4972** | **0.0000** |

A **16-point spread on a 0–100 oscillator** — the difference between reading oversold and
overbought — with no error, no NaN and a plausible number at every length. This is the prior
system's *"same market, different score"* reproduced exactly, in TA-Lib.

**Two traps this exposes:**

1. **TA-Lib's own `lookback` is not a warm-up figure.** It reports RSI 14, ATR 14, MACD 33,
   STOCHRSI 20, EMA(200) 199. Those are the *mechanical floor* — the inputs consumed before any
   output exists. Taking them as `required_bars` gives RSI 14 bars and a value 12 points wrong.
2. **The unstable period defaults to 0**, so TA-Lib strips nothing and warns nothing. A 30-bar
   RSI array returns a confident float at index 14.

**Therefore:** recursive indicators (RSI, ATR, EMA, StochRSI, **and MACD**, which TA-Lib does
*not* annotate despite its EMA-26 core) declare **250 bars**. Convergence arrives near 150 in
this measurement; 250 is deliberate headroom. Non-recursive indicators (Bollinger, OBV) declare
their own smaller honest N.

The exactly-N contract from PRD-002 is what makes this safe: a cache growing from 30 bars to 150
would otherwise walk RSI from 63.9 to 59.5 over weeks, silently.

## 5. Fallbacks are different indicators

If a value cannot be obtained from its declared source, the answer is `UNAVAILABLE` — **not a
substitute source under the same label.** The prior system silently swapped FRED's `DTWEXBGS`
(26 currencies, weekly, lagged) for yfinance's `DX-Y.NYB` (6 currencies, real-time) behind one
"DXY" label; the value jumped discontinuously whenever the fallback engaged and nothing
recorded which had produced it.

A second source is a second registry entry with its own key, displayed as its own series, or
it does not exist.

## 6. Rendering

TypeScript mirrors the union, with an exhaustive `switch` and a `never` fallthrough so an
unhandled status is a **compile error**:

```ts
type Datapoint =
  | { status: "OK";          value: number; sourceTimestamp: string }
  | { status: "STALE";       value: number; sourceTimestamp: string }
  | { status: "UNAVAILABLE"; reason: Reason }
  | { status: "ERROR";       reason: Reason; detail: string };
```

- `UNAVAILABLE` renders an em dash and its reason. **Never `0`. Never blank.**
- `STALE` renders the value **with its age and a visible stale treatment** — shown, but never
  shown as if current.
- Provenance (vendor, endpoint, source timestamp) is on the face of the value, not behind a
  click.
- No "last known good" fallback that silently presents an older value as current.

# Mobile & PWA

> Mobile & PWA is the layer that extends a web product onto phones and tablets, either by making your existing site installable and offline-capable (a Progressive Web App) or by shipping a real app to the Apple App Store and Google Play built from a shared codebase (React Native, Expo, Flutter, Capacitor, etc.). than by a validation check that could itself have a gap.

```markdown
# 10-research.md — PRD-006-derivatives

## What we already knew, and whether it still holds

| Claim from our knowledge base | Still true? | What the source says | Citation |
|---|---|---|---|
| OKX is reachable from GitHub-hosted (US) runners; Binance and Bybit are not, for derivatives data | **Holds, and independently corroborated for Binance futures specifically** | A GCP US-IP user gets HTTP 451 from `fapi.binance.com` on unauthenticated, no-auth-needed public endpoints — "Any call to https://fapi.binance.com/fapi/(...) returns an HTTP 451 error," confirmed as IP-based geoblocking, not an account restriction | https://dev.binance.vision/t/error-451-when-accessing-the-futures-api-from-us/16725 |
| Funding intervals are dynamic and not fixed at 8h — OKX/Bybit can switch | **Holds, and now precisely characterized** — this PRD's central risk has an exact mechanism | OKX's automatic frequency adjustment: "When the funding rate reaches its cap or floor at settlement, the frequency will be escalated by one level at a time" — an explicit **8h → 4h → 2h → 1h** ladder, reverting only after "the funding rate at every settlement during the preceding 12 consecutive hours was within ±0.20%." OKX also manually re-tiered five named instruments from 8h to 4h in named 2024 announcements, independent of the automatic mechanism | https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/okx-to-enable-automatic-updates-for-funding-fee-settlement-period ; https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/okx-to-adjust-funding-rate-interval-for-certain-perpetual-futures |
| Vendors expose a live/predicted funding number distinct from settled funding, and blurring them is a trap | **Holds** — OKX's public docs and third-party engineering writeups treat `GET /public/funding-rate` (current + upcoming predicted rate) and `GET /public/funding-rate-history` (settled, historical) as genuinely separate endpoints with separate semantics | https://github.com/tiagosiebler/okx-api/blob/master/docs/endpointFunctionList.md |
| Coin-margined (inverse) vs USDT-margined (linear) OI is a unit-mixing trap | **Holds** | OKX names its non-USDT products "crypto-margined perpetual futures... settled in cryptocurrencies like BTC, with a contract size of 100 USD" against USDT-margined contracts settled in USDT — i.e. the same instrument family exists in both a coin-denominated and a USD-denominated form and nothing in the wire format stops you from summing across them | https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/i-perpetual-swaps (via search synthesis — see note below) |
| **Our knowledge base does NOT already know the exact endpoint the settlement interval must be read from** — it says "record it" but not where the source of truth is | **Gap, now closed** | There is **no dedicated field for "current interval" on the historical funding-rate-history payload itself**. OKX's own guidance for finding the *current* interval is to hit `GET /api/v5/public/funding-rate` (the live/predicted endpoint) or the web UI — "refer to the Perpetual Contract Information page or the API endpoint...for the latest settlement frequency, and adjust your trading strategies accordingly." The settled-history endpoint (`funding-rate-history`) returns only `fundingTime`/`fundingRate` per record — the interval for a *historical* record must be **derived from the gap between consecutive `fundingTime` values**, not read from a field | https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/okx-to-enable-automatic-updates-for-funding-fee-settlement-period |
| Long/short ratio and taker-ratio history depth may be capped (R1 flagged Binance's 30-day rolling cap; OKX's equivalent limit unconfirmed) | **Partially resolved, still a genuine open question** | Third-party SDK docs confirm OKX's `rubik/stat` family (open-interest-volume, taker-volume, long-short-account-ratio) all take `period`/`begin`/`end`/`limit` params, but no source found in this research pass states OKX's own retention ceiling in days. The parallel, better-documented `funding-rate-history` endpoint **is capped at 400 records** (≈1 year at 8h cadence) — this is the closest confirmed analog and the working assumption should be that `rubik/stat` endpoints have a comparable, not unlimited, retention window, to be confirmed empirically in the reachability spike rather than assumed | https://www.holysheep.cn/articles/en-okx-funding-rate-history-api-for-backtesting-2026-07-12-0017.html |

## Existing implementations

- **`tiagosiebler/okx-api`** (TypeScript, actively maintained, used widely as the reference for the full v5 surface) exposes each endpoint this PRD needs as a distinct typed function: `getFundingRate()`, `getFundingRateHistory()`, `getOpenInterest()`, `getContractsOpenInterestAndVolume()`, `getTakerVolume()`, `getContractTakerVolume()`, `getLongShortRatio()`, `getLongShortContractRatio()` — all public, no auth, GET-only. Confirms the shape this PRD's fetchers should mirror one endpoint per registry entry, not one combined call. https://github.com/tiagosiebler/okx-api/blob/master/docs/endpointFunctionList.md
- **`okxapi/python-okx`** — the Python reference SDK — hardcodes the same literal paths (`/api/v5/public/funding-rate`, `/api/v5/public/funding-rate-history`, `/api/v5/public/open-interest`, `/api/v5/rubik/stat/taker-volume`, `/api/v5/rubik/stat/contracts/long-short-account-ratio`) as constants, useful directly since this project's ingestion is already Python/httpx. https://github.com/okxapi/python-okx (consts.py)
- **HolySheep AI's backtesting engineering guide** is an existing practitioner writeup of exactly this PRD's funding-history ingestion problem: it hits `limit=100`/page, paginates on `fundingTime` via `after`, warns "OKX caps at 100/page" and that the total series is capped at "400 records (≈1 year for 8h funding cadence)," and separately warns that `before`/`after` pagination "is brittle for multi-symbol sweeps" — worth taking as a direct implementation constraint rather than re-discovering it via trial and error. https://www.holysheep.cn/articles/en-okx-funding-rate-history-api-for-backtesting-2026-07-12-0017.html

## Approach options

**A. OKX-only, single-venue, "uncorroborated" declared per US-306** — Fetch funding/OI/long-short/taker from OKX only, mark every derivatives registry entry as uncorroborated (structurally already legal per PRD-003/US-306). *Trade-off:* simplest, ships fastest, zero cross-venue reconciliation logic, but the registry carries a permanent "single source of truth" flag for this whole category — acceptable for a personal dashboard, not for anything claiming institutional-grade data quality. *Cost:* $0, one venue's rate limits only. *Who uses it:* small personal dashboards and single-exchange trading bots (implicit in every SDK surveyed — none of the surveyed OSS clients wrap more than one venue's derivatives endpoints in a single call).

**B. OKX primary + Coinglass (or similar aggregator) as second source for corroboration only** — OKX stays the fetched-and-displayed value; a second call to an aggregator checks the OKX number is in the same order of magnitude, without displaying the aggregator's (often modeled) number. *Trade-off:* satisfies US-306's "declare a second source" requirement with an actual second source rather than a flag, but Coinglass's own numbers for exactly this category (long/short, OI) are partly derived/modeled per this project's own prior finding on liquidations — using it even just for corroboration risks importing that same "modeled passing as measured" problem this PRD explicitly refuses. *Cost:* Coinglass free tier is rate-limited and its API terms/availability weren't verified in this pass — flag as **UNVERIFIED**, needs its own reachability check before committing. *Who uses it:* aggregator-dependent retail dashboards (Coinglass's own product is the canonical example of this pattern, per the coinglass.com references surfaced throughout this research pass, e.g. https://www.coinglass.com/exchanges/OKX).

**C. Two-venue direct: OKX + a genuinely reachable second exchange (e.g. Coinbase or Kraken derivatives, if they expose funding/OI at all), fully independent fetch-and-compare** — the gold-standard version of what PRD-003 asks for. *Trade-off:* Coinbase and Kraken's perpetual/derivatives products and public API surface for funding/OI/long-short were **not verified in this research pass** — this project's existing architecture doc only measured their *spot* OHLCV reachability, not their derivatives endpoints, so this option carries real unresolved risk that a second venue simply doesn't expose these fields publicly. *Cost:* unknown until endpoint existence is confirmed. *Who uses it:* institutional data vendors (Kaiko, Amberdata), not solo/small-team dashboards, per the general pattern across every practitioner source surveyed.

**Recommendation: Option A now, structured so Option B/C is a additive registry-entry change later.** Every source found in this pass — the SDK doc, the backtesting guide, OKX's own docs — treats OKX's derivatives surface as complete and self-consistent for BTC/ETH/SOL/BNB perpetuals; no second venue's derivatives endpoints were confirmed reachable or even existent in this research window, and PRD-003/US-306 already makes "declared uncorroborated" a legal, non-blocking state rather than a gap that has to be silently papered over.

## Edge cases and gotchas

- **The historical funding-rate endpoint carries no interval field — you must derive it from consecutive `fundingTime` deltas, or you will silently inherit the annualization bug this PRD exists to prevent.** OKX's own guidance for the *current* interval points to a *different* endpoint (`GET /public/funding-rate`, the live one this PRD deliberately does not fetch for display) or the web UI — nothing in the settled-history payload states the interval directly. A naive implementation that fetches `funding-rate-history` and assumes 8h will be wrong for exactly the tiered instruments OKX names by name. https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/okx-to-enable-automatic-updates-for-funding-fee-settlement-period
- **Backtesting-focused engineering writeups treating OKX in 2026 still hardcode "8h" without checking it.** The most detailed practitioner guide found in this pass — written specifically about funding-rate history for backtesting — states flatly "Funding rate — settled every 8 hours" as a fixed constant throughout its examples, with zero handling for interval changes. This is a live demonstration that the exact bug this PRD's adversarial case targets is not a hypothetical — a specialist writeup published in 2026 makes it. https://www.holysheep.cn/articles/en-okx-v5-api-yanshengpin-funding-rate-yu-mark-price--2026-07-18-0005.html
- **`funding-rate-history` is capped at 400 records total (≈1 year at 8h cadence), not a rolling window you can page through indefinitely, and pagination via `before`/`after` is "brittle for multi-symbol sweeps."** For BNB or other lower-liquidity instruments whose interval sometimes drops to 1h, 400 records covers far less real time than a year — the retention window is record-count-based, not time-based, so an instrument's own switch to a shorter interval silently shrinks its available history depth. https://www.holysheep.cn/articles/en-okx-funding-rate-history-api-for-backtesting-2026-07-12-0017.html
- **OKX's escalation ladder both tightens (8h→4h→2h→1h) *and* reverts, based on a rolling 12-hour lookback of settlements within ±0.20%** — meaning a single instrument can legitimately show 8h, 4h, 1h, then back to 8h within weeks. Any registry design that treats "funding interval" as a fixed per-instrument attribute set once at onboarding will drift stale silently. https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/okx-to-enable-automatic-updates-for-funding-fee-settlement-period
- **Binance's HTTP 451 to US IPs applies to unauthenticated, no-auth-required public market-data calls specifically on the futures/derivatives API (`fapi.binance.com`)**, not just trading/account endpoints — confirming this PRD cannot fall back to Binance for derivatives from the same US GitHub-hosted compute already chosen for the rest of the project, reinforcing rather than merely repeating the existing architecture decision. https://dev.binance.vision/t/error-451-when-accessing-the-futures-api-from-us/16725

## Services and keys this PRD needs

| Service | Why | Env var | Already provisioned? |
|---|---|---|---|
| OKX public API | Funding rate (settled), OI, long/short ratio, taker ratio — all public, no auth required per every SDK surveyed | none required (public endpoints) | Yes — already integrated for spot/OHLCV per current architecture |

No new keys or secrets are needed for Option A (OKX-only). If Option B/C is later adopted for a second corroboration venue, that venue's key/rate-limit requirements are unverified and must be researched separately before being added here.

## Open questions for the human

| Question | My hypothesis | Impact if wrong | Rank |
|---|---|---|---|
| Does OKX's `rubik/stat` family (OI-volume, taker-volume, long-short-ratio) have a documented retention ceiling, or is it genuinely unbounded? | **UNVERIFIED** hypothesis: it mirrors `funding-rate-history`'s pattern of a hard record-count cap rather than being unbounded, likely on the order of a year or less at the shortest available `period` granularity — must be confirmed empirically against the live endpoint before backfill design is finalized | If wrong (endpoint is actually unbounded), the backfill design is unnecessarily conservative — low cost. If wrong the other way (cap is much shorter than assumed), a backfill story could silently under-deliver history depth without erroring | 1 |
| Should the board standardize on USDT-margined (linear) perpetuals for all four assets, given BNB has no natively obvious coin-margined equivalent anyway? | Yes — USDT-margined for BTC/ETH/SOL/BNB uniformly, since it's the more liquid, more uniformly-available product line across all four assets and avoids the coin/USD unit-mixing trap by construction rather than by validation | If wrong, some instrument's OI values are silently in a different denomination than the other three, defeating the registry-note discipline this PRD calls for | 2 |
| Is a second venue for derivatives corroboration reachable at all from GitHub-hosted US compute, or does US-306's "declare uncorroborated" apply to the whole category permanently? | Uncorroborated-and-declared (Option A) for v1 — no second venue's derivatives public endpoints were confirmed to exist, let alone be reachable, in this research pass | If a second venue turns out to be trivially available later, this is a missed cheap win, not a correctness risk — low cost either way | 3 |

## Blind spots

1. **The registry's "funding interval" field will be correct at write-time and wrong by the next fetch if the escalation/de-escalation ladder isn't re-checked on every ingest, not just at onboarding.** OKX's mechanism explicitly reverts after 12 hours of stable settlements — a field set once and never re-derived from live `fundingTime` deltas will drift the same way the prior system's "confident 0.0" drifted, just more subtly, because it will look plausible rather than obviously blank.
2. **`rubik/stat` endpoints (OI-volume, long-short-ratio, taker-volume) were not confirmed in this research pass to distinguish linear from inverse contracts in their response payload the same way `open-interest`/instrument IDs do.** If the aggregate stat endpoints blend `instType=SWAP` across both margin types under the hood — which was not ruled out here — the unit-mixing trap this PRD names explicitly for raw OI could reappear one layer up, inside an OKX-computed ratio the fetcher never gets to inspect or split.
3. **Nobody has checked whether OKX's rate limits on the `rubik/stat` family (distinct from the 20 req/s figure confirmed only for the public funding endpoint) can sustain four assets × four metrics on the existing GitHub Actions cron cadence without throttling** — a throttling failure here would not look like an outage, it would look like intermittently missing rows, which is exactly the failure mode PRD-005's completeness matrix was built to catch, but only if this PRD's fetchers report it as missing rather than silently retrying into a 429 that gets treated as a transient error and dropped.

## Sources

- https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/okx-to-adjust-funding-rate-interval-for-certain-perpetual-futures

- https://www.okx.com/docs-v5/log_en/
- https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/i-perpetual-swaps
```
